name: preserve-explicit-zero
description: Preserve an explicitly valid zero when defaulting JavaScript numeric options whose contract treats only null or undefined as missing.
applies_when: A JavaScript numeric option explicitly accepts zero, and only null or undefined means the option was omitted.
do_not_apply_when: The contract intentionally treats all falsy values as missing, or the value has not passed the required type validation.
The language has different defaulting semantics; do not perform a blind cross-language operator replacement.

rules.instruction: For this contract, default with nullish coalescing instead of logical OR so that a valid zero survives. Retain the task-specific fallback value and existing type validation.
rules.rationale: Logical OR replaces zero. Nullish coalescing only replaces null or undefined. The fallback 3 belongs to the demonstrated retry setting and is not a universal default.

example.scenario: A separate timeout option accepts timeoutMs=0 to disable the timeout and uses 1000 only when omitted.
example.expected_behavior: After validating the numeric input, options.timeoutMs ?? 1000 preserves 0 and uses 1000 for undefined; keep its own fallback rather than copying the retry default.

counterexample.scenario: A display label intentionally falls back when the input is an empty string.
counterexample.expected_behavior: Do not replace name || 'Anonymous' with nullish coalescing: the empty-string fallback is part of this different contract.
